_comment: Every group of 2+ ref/method rows that legitimately share the exact same (analyte, sex, age, preg) key — found by Stage 2a's collision check. These are NOT classification errors: each row genuinely applies to the same coarse demographic bucket, distinguished only by a clinical condition the sex/age/preg chips don't express (a finer age band, menstrual-cycle phase, time of draw, specimen type, or another one-off covariate). bestRange() in shell.html used to pick one of these silently, by array order, whenever none scored higher than the others — the same class of silent-wrong-value risk as the original My Lab bug, just in the interpreter's row-picker instead of the override store. The fix: the Result Interpreter now detects a tie against this list and makes the user pick which row applies, by its own grp label, instead of guessing (see activeRange()/bestRange() and renderInterp() in shell.html). qa/validate_ties.js fails the build if a NEW, unlisted tie shows up among ref/method rows for any test — the same append-only-review discipline as qa/validate_rids.js, so a future content update can't silently reintroduce a guessed pick without a human looking at it first.

_dimension_summary.age-subband: A single age bucket (adult, neonate) is too coarse — the real reference interval changes within it (ESR by decade, IGF-1 by decade, testosterone by decade, PSA by decade, cystatin ≥60y, bilirubin by hours-of-life, ammonia preterm/sick-neonate).
_dimension_summary.cycle-phase: Reproductive hormones vary by menstrual-cycle phase or menopausal status, which the sex/age/preg chips don't capture (LH, FSH, estradiol, progesterone, 17-OHP, and bone turnover markers by meno status).
_dimension_summary.timing: Same analyte, same patient, different expected value depending on WHEN or under what test condition it's drawn (cortisol/ACTH by time of day, glucose random vs post-prandial).
_dimension_summary.one_off_covariate: A single extra covariate with no other home in the schema (lactate venous vs arterial specimen, vWF by ABO blood group, CEA by smoking status, Bence Jones ratio by renal function).

groups._why: Found by qa/test5.py, not the original ref/method-only collision scan — these two rows are both kind=cutoff, not ref/method, but the same silent-wrong-pick risk applies: a D-dimer drawn from someone over 50 must be read against the age-adjusted cutoff (r2), not the <50y exclusion cutoff (r1). This is the first confirmation that the tie list isn't limited to ref/method rows; most of the ~130 other same-key groups among dx/cutoff/target rows across the corpus are value-ordered severity ladders (e.g. vitamin D deficient/insufficient/sufficient/toxic), which need a different fix — grading the entered value against the ladder, not asking the user to pre-pick a row — tracked separately as the kind-aware-interpreter stage, not solved by this file.
